# Bartender4

## [4.19.2](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/tree/4.19.2) (2026-11-18)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/compare/4.19.1...4.19.2) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/releases)

- Fix the quest XP of the XP bar in a few edge cases  
    The rested XP is shown up to the end of the bar on clients which show it  
    when it reaches beyond the level, a quest which was turned in is forgotten  
    even while the XP bar is not shown, the level up animation is reset when it  
    was interrupted, and nothing is done at all while the quest XP is disabled.

# Bartender4

## [4.19.1](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/tree/4.19.1) (2026-11-18)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/compare/4.19.0...4.19.1) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/releases)

- Show the XP of completed quests on the status tracking bar  
    The XP bar can show the XP of the quests which are ready to be turned in,  
    as a segment following the XP.  
    The option is off by default.  
    The manager and the containers of the status tracking bar are given global  
    names, so other addons can find the bars more easily.  
- Make the bag buttons immune to the layout of the Blizzard bags bar  
    The bags bar of the Blizzard UI anchors every bag button to itself  
    whenever it runs its layout, which happens on every update of the edit  
    mode layout and when the bag bar expands or collapses. The module used  
    to move the buttons back from a hook on that layout function. A layout  
    that did not go through the hooked function, or that failed part way,  
    left the buttons at the position of the hidden Blizzard bar until the  
    UI was reloaded. This was seen on WoW Forever after releasing through a  
    loading screen, the call that got past the hook was not identified.  
    The buttons are now detached once, when the bar is created: their  
    SetPoint and ClearAllPoints do nothing, and the bar positions them  
    through the original functions of their frame type. The hook on the  
    layout and the removal of the expand callback are no longer needed.  
    The keyring is reset to the horizontal orientation and no longer follows  
    the orientation of the edit mode, which rotated and resized it on the  
    bar.  
    Buttons that are not on the bar are parked on the hidden frame, instead  
    of hidden in the center of the screen or left without anchors. The  
    classic clients show the keyring again on every bag update.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Remove unused symbols from the luacheck configuration  
- Remove dead compat code from the MicroMenu module  
    MicroMenu, MicroMenuContainer and C\_PetBattles exist on every supported  
    client, and UpdateMicroButtonsParent on none of them. Drop the checks and  
    the code which only the UpdateMicroButtonsParent hook could reach.  
- Remove compat shims for APIs available on all clients  
- Remove the upvalues of Lua and API functions  
    None of them were used in a hot code path, so they only added noise.  
- Remove the old GLOBALS comment blocks  
- Make the extra ability container immune to the edit mode  
    The container of the extra action button and the zone abilities is a  
    system of the edit mode, and a frame that the frame position management  
    of the Blizzard UI places. Both move and reparent it, also in combat.  
    The module used to undo that from hooks, which is not possible in combat  
    and was never repeated afterwards. The cleanup of the frame position  
    management also used a name that only exists on the classic clients, so  
    on Retail and Forever the container could be pulled off the bar.  
    The container is now detached once, when the bar is created: it is taken  
    out of the frame position management, and its SetPoint and ClearAllPoints  
    do nothing, so the anchors of the edit mode have no effect. The bar  
    positions it through the original functions, which the edit mode keeps as  
    SetPointBase and ClearAllPointsBase.

# Bartender4

## [4.19.0](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/tree/4.19.0) (2026-11-16)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/compare/4.18.4.1...4.19.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Bartender4/releases)

- Replace the Blizzard status tracking bars with a custom implementation  
    The module used to reparent Blizzard's StatusTrackingBarManager into a  
    Bartender bar and disable its edit mode behaviour. It now owns its manager  
    and both bar containers, and no longer touches the Blizzard manager, its  
    containers or the edit mode.  
    Only the leaf bar templates are still taken from Blizzard, since they hold  
    the per-client rules for experience, reputation, honor, artifact, azerite  
    and house favor.  
- Add the totem bar to the WoW Forever presets  
    The totem bar takes the place of the stance bar, as no class has both.  
    In the three bars stacked preset, which has no stance bar, it sits above  
    the action bars with the pet bar moved up above it.  
- Add key bindings and readable binding names for the totem bar  
    The buttons are listed in the key binding UI of WoW Forever through a  
    separate bindings file, and show the same names in LibKeyBound.  
    The totem buttons are numbered in the order they are shown in (earth,  
    fire, water, air), which differs from the order of the totem slots their  
    frame names are based on.  
- Remove the classic XP and Reputation bar modules  
    All classic clients have moved to the StatusTrackingBarManager, so the  
    MainMenuExpBar and ReputationWatchBar frames these modules wrapped no  
    longer exist on any client.  
- Replace the Blizzard totem bar with a fully custom implementation  
    The old module reparented the protected MultiCastActionBarFrame, which  
    EditMode repositions in combat, where it cannot be moved back.  
    The new bar is built from LibActionButton buttons for summon, the four  
    totems and recall, with secure flyouts to assign totems and to switch  
    between the summon spells. As a ButtonBar it supports padding, growth  
    direction, zoom and the other button options.  
    It is only loaded in WoW Forever for now. The settings of the old module  
    are reused, so the bar keeps its position.  
- Let bars report mouse over content outside of their overlay  
    A bar can implement IsMouseOverContent to count additional frames as  
    part of the bar for the mouse-over fade, eg. flyouts that extend beyond  
    the bar overlay.  
- Add a button margin and a fixed button count to the ButtonBar layout  
    button\_margin reserves space around every button for art that extends  
    beyond the button frame, so that the bar overlay covers it.  
    fixed\_button\_count sizes the bar for a set number of buttons instead of  
    the number of buttons currently shown, so a bar keeps its size while its  
    buttons come and go.  
    Both default to the previous behavior for all existing bars.  
- Implement a fully custom vehicle button  
    Stop reusing the vanilla button, as its encumbered with EditMode hooks  
    and can cause taint issues depending on how its anchored.  
    None of the vehicle functions are protected, so this button is a lot  
    simpler and avoids one source of bugs.
